1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of __modulated IR radiation__ light pulses having a first speed; receiving __, via an IR video sensor,__ a second sequence of __modulated IR radiation__ light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of __modulated IR radiation__ light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the __computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, the second speed being__ different from the first speed, __and wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history, or vehicle status, encoded into the light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed__.

2. (Cancelled)

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the __third__ vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed.

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Cancelled)

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Cancelled)

9. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Previously presented) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses.
